dispositions.area: Local email/password identity, session and abuse controls
dispositions.evidence: Current implementation already uses scrypt, hashed session/CSRF tokens, strict cookies, origin/CSRF checks, bounded sessions, revocation and persisted throttling with focused regression coverage.
Manual Zod parsing currently escapes through NestJS as HTTP 500. Add a narrow privacy-safe 400 mapping and deterministic controller regression coverage without weakening anti-enumeration.
Current source contains a truthful Can’t sign in disclosure, while the deployed web artifact predates it. Preserve DEC-038 and improve test coverage; do not add a reset or transfer success path.

dispositions.area: External identity, passkeys and password recovery
dispositions.evidence: The approved fail-closed unavailable boundary remains authoritative. Provider configuration does not activate adapters, and no recovery route may be invented by this defect repair.

Retain the existing Container Apps, reverse proxy, managed identity, synthetic Azure Files and Bicep model; replace stale web/API images with immutable exact-candidate artifacts after QA and retain one DEV API replica so interactive account entry does not wait on scale-to-zero.

The current quality workflow runs specification/PostgreSQL, Android and macOS iOS jobs for every PR with no changed-path classification. A separate governed change should preserve required check names while routing expensive component work by affected paths.

consultations: ORCH-015: governed scope, release gates and separation from active Story P1-009
DEV-WEB-004: focused Web/API implementation and regression evidence
OPS-001: read-only CI efficiency and provenance analysis
Independent QA role reserved for an isolated exact-candidate retest after implementation
risks: Creating a working forgot-password path would violate approved DEC-038 and could introduce a weaker account/workspace/key takeover route.
A healthy GET session endpoint does not prove registration/login writes; exact-candidate and deployed synthetic end-to-end smoke evidence are required.
The DEV Azure Files identity state is synthetic but persistent; smoke fixtures must be unique, non-personal and privacy-safe.

Keeping one 0.5 vCPU / 1 GiB DEV API replica continuously available increases Azure Container Apps cost; exact AUD impact is provider/usage dependent and remains UNAVAILABLE until billing evidence is observed.
Deploying directly without updating immutable Bicep image references would create configuration drift.
Changing test routing in the authentication repair would make product acceptance harder to attribute and could weaken branch protection.
recommendation: Repair auth validation, bounded startup/retry behavior and recovery-unavailable presentation; retain one DEV API replica; pass focused and protected exact-candidate QA; build immutable candidate images; update reviewed DEV image references; deploy through Bicep; and prove registration/logout/login in DEV with synthetic data. Create a separate governed CI-routing item from OPS-001 evidence rather than weakening this repair's gates.
